channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Iran War Has Cost US Military $48.3 Billion, Pentagon Tells Senators
item.description: The war against Iran has cost the United States military $48.3 billion, a senior Pentagon budget official told senators on Thursday, in the first official update of the war's price in more than a month.

item.title: Trump Threatens 'Tremendous Tax' on US Firms Building AI Data Centres Abroad
item.description: President Donald Trump has said the United States will not allow American companies to build data centres in other countries, threatening them with a heavy tax if they do, in a move aimed at keeping the artificial intelligence race on American soil.

item.title: Magnitude 6.9 Earthquake Shakes Peru's Andes, Tremors Felt in Lima
item.description: Central Peru was shaken by a strong earthquake on Friday evening, and people in the capital Lima felt the tremors and ran out into the streets. Officials said there were no immediate reports of damage or anyone hurt.

item.title: Russian Ballistic Missiles Kill a Child and a Paramedic in Kryvyi Rih, Wounding 42
item.description: Two ballistic missiles fired by Russia hit the centre of Kryvyi Rih on Friday evening. A seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman working as a paramedic were killed, and 42 people were wounded, local officials said.

item.title: Africa's New Credit Rating Agency Aims to Rewrite How the Continent Is Judged
item.description: Africa now has its own credit rating agency, launched to challenge the three Western firms that decide what the continent's governments pay to borrow, after years of complaints that their ratings overstate African risk.

item.title: Saudi Defences Down Three Houthi Missiles Over Riyadh on Third Night of Alerts
item.description: Saudi air defences intercepted three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh in the early hours of Saturday, the Saudi-led coalition said, as emergency alerts sounded in the capital for a third night in a row.

item.title: French Senate Approves Police Shootings Law Critics Call a 'Licence to Kill'
item.description: France's Senate has given final approval to a law that presumes police officers who fire their weapons acted within the law, a measure critics describe as a licence to kill and left-wing lawmakers plan to challenge in court.

item.title: Overcrowded Funeral Boat Capsizes in Nigeria, Killing at Least Four
item.description: An overcrowded boat carrying mourners to a funeral capsized in southern Nigeria on Friday, killing at least four people, including two children, police said, as rescuers searched waters where residents fear hundreds may still be missing.

item.title: Anthropic Researcher Says AI Has Proved the Riemann Hypothesis, Maths' Greatest Unsolved Problem
item.description: A mathematician at Anthropic says he has used the company's AI system Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, the most famous unsolved problem in mathematics, in a claim that has not yet been independently verified.

item.title: Denmark Expels Russian Defence Attache Over Alleged Plot to Kill Ukrainian Rapper
item.description: Denmark has accused Russian intelligence of plotting to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner on Danish soil and ordered Russia's defence attache in Copenhagen to leave the country within seven days.

item.title: S&P 500 and Dow Join Nasdaq in Correction as AI Sell-Off Wipes Out the Year's Gains
item.description: The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed in correction territory on Friday, joining the Nasdaq after a brutal week in which the tech-heavy index erased all of its gains for 2026.

item.title: France Probes Depardieu and Houellebecq Over Alleged Gang Rape on Film Set
item.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into actor Gérard Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq over allegations that an actress was gang-raped and sexually assaulted during the filming of the 2018 movie 'Thalasso', in the latest case to shake French cinema.

item.title: Two Salvadoran Soldiers Killed in Haiti Blast in First Deaths of Deployment
item.description: Two Salvadoran soldiers were killed and two more injured in a blast while handling explosive material during their deployment in Haiti, El Salvador's military said on Friday, in the first officially reported deaths since the large-scale deployment began about a month ago.

item.title: Seven Killed in Israeli Drone Strikes Across Central Gaza as Ceasefire Frays
item.description: At least seven Palestinians were killed and others wounded in Israeli drone strikes across central Gaza on Friday, medical sources said, as attacks continued despite a ceasefire that has formally been in force for more than a year.

item.title: Anti-Hamas Palestinian Groups Accused of Taking Part in Israeli Gaza Operation
item.description: Palestinian security sources say Israeli-backed local armed groups took part in this week's Israeli ground operation in central Gaza, pressing families to flee their homes under the cover of Israeli fire.

item.title: Nepal's Fans Turn Doha Into a Home Crowd as Their Team's Global Rise Rolls On
item.description: Thousands of Nepali fans turned a stadium in Doha into a home crowd on Friday as Nepal's cricket team continued its climb among Asia's best at the Rising Stars Asia Cup.

item.title: Iraqi Forces Enter Kataib Hezbollah Stronghold in Deal After Oil-Smuggling Standoff
item.description: Iraqi security forces have entered Jurf al-Sakhar, the stronghold of the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah armed group, under a compromise deal that ends a standoff over alleged oil smuggling and restores state control to an area closed to government forces for about 12 years.

item.title: Trump Tells Europe Putin Is 'Tired' and Ready for a Ukraine Deal
item.description: Donald Trump told European leaders on Thursday that Vladimir Putin is tired of the war in Ukraine and ready to make a deal, urging them to seize the opening even as Russia launched a massive overnight barrage on Kyiv hours later.

item.title: Indian Man Gets 19 Years in US Prison for Plot to Kill Sikh Separatist in New York
item.description: A United States federal judge on Friday sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to more than 19 years in prison for his part in a failed plan to kill a Sikh separatist leader on American soil, closing a case that has strained relations between Washington and New Delhi.

item.title: Trump Vows Tremendous Tax for US Firms Building Data Centers Abroad
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Friday that US technology companies will face a "tremendous tax" if they build artificial intelligence data centers in other countries, in a move he said was aimed at keeping the facilities, and the AI race with China, on American soil.

item.title: Anthropic Shares Slide Toward IPO Price as AI Sell-Off Deepens
item.description: Anthropic shares fell sharply on their second day of trading on Friday, sliding toward their $83 listing price as a wider sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks deepened.

item.title: Qatar Emir Pledges 15bn Euros in Germany as Berlin Visit Pushes Diplomacy to End Iran War
item.description: Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani pledged an additional 15 billion euros in investment in Germany on Friday, as his first visit to Berlin in 16 years put diplomacy to end the war with Iran at the top of the agenda.

item.title: Young People March Across Europe in Day of Action Over Living Costs and War Spending
item.description: Tens of thousands of young people marched across Europe on Friday in a coordinated day of action spanning more than 25 countries, demanding relief from the rising cost of living, more funding for schools and universities, and an end to higher military spending.

item.title: Tanker Hit in Strait of Hormuz as Doubt Grows Over Iran's Blockade-Busting Convoy
item.description: A tanker has caught fire after being hit in the Strait of Hormuz, as doubt grows over Iran's reported plan to send a loaded convoy past the United States naval blockade of its oil exports.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Shoots Down Five Houthi Drones and a Missile as Riyadh Comes Under Fire
item.description: Saudi air defences shot down five Houthi drones and a ballistic missile on Friday, and later intercepted two more ballistic missiles headed for the Jazan region, as the Saudi-led coalition pressed its strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen, including seven military sites in Sanaa.

item.title: White House Cyber Director Cairncross Is Out After Week of Tech Outages
item.description: Sean Cairncross, the White House official who coordinated the federal government's cybersecurity policy, is leaving his post after a week of technology outages that disrupted air travel, banking and government systems, officials confirmed on Thursday.

item.title: US Small Firms Feel the Squeeze as War Pushes Fuel and Commodity Costs Higher
item.description: American small businesses are facing a sharp rise in fuel and commodity costs as the fallout from the war in Iran spreads beyond energy markets, new Bank of America data shows.

item.title: South Africa Moves Ahead With 5.2 GW Nuclear Build, First New Reactors in Decades
item.description: South Africa is pressing ahead with plans for 5,200 megawatts of new nuclear power, its biggest atomic programme since the Koeberg plant was built more than four decades ago.

item.title: Trump Says Vance Got It Wrong on the Iran War as Questions Grow Over His Deputy
item.description: President Donald Trump has said Vice President JD Vance erred in how he talked about the war with Iran, as questions grow about the vice president's standing after the midterm elections.

item.title: Tusk Calls Russian Missile Crash in Poland a Deliberate Provocation
item.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has called the Russian missiles and drone that crashed in Poland a deliberate provocation, saying it was no coincidence they fell beside a major Western military exercise.
